title: Bittensor Daily News: November 27, 2026

updates.headline: SN6 Numinous v4.2.0 changes forecasts to 31-part probability distributions
updates.summary: In a November 25 changelog update, Numinous introduced a new forecast format: probabilities for each of the next 30 days plus an outcome for an event not occurring within that period. The shares must be normalized. Scoring compares the submitted distribution with a house forecast using a ranked-probability-score approach, rather than rewarding a single predicted date. Existing submissions continue under their original rules until their 30-day windows end, but new submissions in the old format are rejected under the new release. This is a dated catch-up on a participation and scoring change, not a claim that the subnet has demonstrated better forecasting results.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: miners face a meaningful submission and scoring change; broader adoption or exceptional results are not established.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Three stars: miners face a meaningful submission and scoring change; broader adoption or exceptional results are not established.
ratingAssessment.uncertainty: Release documentation establishes the specification, not measured forecast improvement.

updates.headline: SN41 Almanac asks holders about a higher owner emissions share
updates.summary:
Almanac is asking SN41 holders whether to raise the owner share of alpha emissions from 10% to 15%, reducing the validators-and-stakers share from 40% to 35% while leaving miners at 50%. The official ballot lists a November 23 opening and December 9, 23:59 UTC close. This is dated catch-up coverage of an open proposal, discussed again by the team on November 26.

The proposed extra allocation would support development of a new market-maker incentive mechanism, tools and onboarding. Votes are weighted by the SN41 alpha held when the question closes. The ballot is advisory: Almanac retains discretion over whether and how to implement the outcome. No allocation change or voting result is confirmed here; the page’s loading-state counters are not a verified tally.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: concrete participation and allocation proposal exceeds minor housekeeping; no enacted change or wider network consequence establishes four.

ratingAssessment.consequence: An advisory ballot proposes moving five percentage points from validators/stakers to owner operations.
ratingAssessment.evidence: Official almnc.ai/vote terms and November 26 moderator link in the official SN41 channel.
ratingAssessment.scope: SN41 holders, validators, stakers and operator.
ratingAssessment.uncertainty: Advisory proposal only; no enacted allocation change or reliable current tally verified.
ratingAssessment.adjacentRatingReason: Three stars: concrete participation and allocation proposal exceeds minor housekeeping; no enacted change or wider network consequence establishes four.

updates.headline: SN49 Nepher names tabletop winners and announces a parts-sorting contest
updates.summary: Nepher’s operator announced approved Phase 2 tabletop challenge winners on November 27: Jonathan Hou scored 0.8273, HugoR1989 0.8204 and Jason Zhu 0.7438. The team reported 20 agents from 15 participants and a 70/20/10 reward split, with rankings based on a private evaluation separate from the public board. A separate November 26 announcement sets out Phase 1 of a parts-sorting challenge: a Franka arm with a Robotiq gripper must sort industrial parts into instructed tray cells across 16 fixed simulation tasks. Submissions are scheduled to open December 5 at 12:28 UTC, with evaluation December 6–7. These are operator-reported competition results and simulation tasks, not proof of customer deployment or verified reward payment.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: concrete results and a new participation window, capped as competition coverage.

updates.headline: SN50 Synth reports live scoring and acknowledges a first-block scoring bug
updates.summary: Synth’s official SN50 Discord channel published a November 27 operating report saying its push endpoint launched November 26 and its scoring ledger went live later that evening. The report counted 115 miner hotkeys with accepted submissions and 63,358 accepted submissions through 14:04 UTC. These are operator-reported activity figures, not an independent audit or proof of profitable trading. In a subsequent reply, the operator acknowledged that a new key’s first scoring block could generate excessive debt and distort other participants’ credit. The announced fix is to give that initial block zero credit and begin scoring once fitting data exists, then recompute blocks that are not final. Deployment of that fix was still pending confirmation at this report’s cutoff. The operator explicitly labels its trading comparison as simulation and says the short sample does not establish an edge.
updates.ratingReason: Four stars: live scoring plus an acknowledged scoring defect and concrete remediation affect miner participation and credits. Exceptional ecosystem-wide consequences are not established.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Live miner scoring and a confirmed operator response to a scoring defect affect participation.

ratingAssessment.adjacentRatingReason: Three understates a launch with a consequential scoring issue; five is not warranted by this bounded early rollout.

updates.headline: SN55 NIOME outlines a rare-disease variant-calling challenge
updates.summary: NIOME outlined a new challenge on November 26 aimed at identifying disease-causing genetic variants and their correct genotypes. Participants would train weights for a fixed DeepVariant architecture, while NIOME handles inference and evaluation. The proposed scoring counts a patient as solved only when all causal variants are identified, includes negative cases to penalize over-calling, and keeps genome-wide accuracy as a guardrail. Each round is intended to use fresh private evaluation data. The initial focus is inherited anaemias. The team’s announcement says launch details are still to come: this is a planned competition, not a clinically validated diagnostic service or a claim of patient outcomes.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: meaningful competition design and participant requirements, subject to the competition ceiling.

updates.headline: SN71 Leadpoet merges an export catch-up fix
updates.summary: Leadpoet merged a November 27 change allowing its existing watcher to process up to three export groups within its current work window. The scheduling uses the previous groupâ€™s duration to leave time for indexing. If a later group is interrupted, completed groups can still be published and progress resumes from the last successful point. Weight-setting and settlement retain priority. This is an operational throughput fix in the repository, not evidence of new customer demand or a change to payouts.

updates.headline: SN120 Affine merges a six-benchmark math dashboard specification
updates.summary: Affine merged a November 25 change specifying six public math benchmarks, each using eight rollouts: three HMMT editions, BRUMO 2025, CMIMC 2025 and BeyondAIME. Dataset revisions, item counts and ordering are pinned, and answers use symbolic grading rather than an LLM judge. A displayed average requires all six scores; a row missing one receives no average. Older benchmark results remain stored even as their columns are retired. The pull request explicitly says it did not perform a production deployment or site publication, so this catch-up covers merged code rather than a confirmed live dashboard change or model-performance breakthrough.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: a substantial evaluation-method and display change; deployment and new model results are not established.

updates.headline: SN121 SundaeBar plans archive-node fix for rejected payment credits
updates.summary: SundaeBar’s operator acknowledged on November 27 that some credit-funded submissions failed payment verification because the validator tried to reread an original payment block whose state the public node had already discarded. The operator says a fix has been built to fall back to an archive node, but deployment is scheduled after SBC40 closes at 17:00 UTC, noon Eastern, rather than during the active challenge. In the reviewed cases, credits were restored with 14-day validity for use in SBC41; the operator said those submissions would not be requeued before the current close. A separate similarity check remains in place. The fix is announced and pending deployment, not a confirmed restoration of every affected submission.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: a verified operator acknowledgement and remedy materially affect miner access to evaluation; broader systemic consequences are not established.

updates.headline: SN124 Swarm sets a 200-second search-and-rescue task for TestField v2
updates.summary: Swarmâ€™s November 26 TestField v2 announcement describes a drone benchmark requiring takeoff, search, reporting and landing within 200 seconds. The task calls for locating people and animals to within one metre, with day, night and thermal conditions, across 1,000 fields per two-week epoch using Andorran terrain. These figures describe the required task, not results already achieved by drones or proof of a field deployment. The update gives participants a clearer operational target for the subnetâ€™s search-and-rescue testing.

ecosystem.headline: TAOApp announces November 30 shutdown and prorated API refunds
ecosystem.summary: TAOApp says it will shut down on Monday, November 30. Its current website also says subscribed API keys will receive prorated refunds. This gives users and developers a concrete migration deadline for a Bittensor data service. The timing is not completely consistent: the website lists 9 AM Eastern, while the November 26 announcement said around 10 AM Eastern. Users should check the operatorâ€™s latest notice rather than assume an extra hour of access. These are announced shutdown and refund plans; completed refunds have not been independently verified.
ecosystem.ratingReason: Four stars: a scheduled data-service closure materially affects dependent users and integrations. Five is not established because this is not a network-wide outage.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Four stars: a scheduled data-service closure materially affects dependent users and integrations. Five is not established because this is not a network-wide outage.
ratingAssessment.uncertainty: Shutdown and refunds are prospective; the exact hour differs between notices.

ecosystem.headline: Subtensor merges a fix for weight commitments during hotkey swaps
ecosystem.summary: A November 26 change merged into Subtensorâ€™s release-498 branch addresses weight commitments that cannot be revealed after a hotkey swap because their hashes are tied to the committing key. The change drops affected pending commitments for the swapped subnets while preserving destination queues and unaffected subnet queues. This is a specific code-level reliability fix for the commit-and-reveal process. A merged pull request does not, by itself, establish that this behavior has been activated on the live chain.
ecosystem.ratingReason: Three stars: a concrete but bounded protocol reliability fix; a live network activation or broad incident is not established.

ecosystem.headline: xTAO reports validator compatibility updates; API product remains in development
ecosystem.summary: In a November 26 issuer release, xTAO said it completed validator updates supporting recent Bittensor network changes, including Gamma and optional wallet features. It also said existing wallets continue to work without a mandatory migration. Its planned API-access product remains in development; the release should not be read as a product launch. This is a dated operational update from the company, not independent verification of validator performance.
